item.title: Fired trans TA appeals OU decision over flunking Bible-based essay
item.description: 'Mel Curth has been the target of a political movement that seeks to silence and/or oust LGBTQ people from academia,' attorney says.

item.title: Amherst erupts after student reporter exposes sex skits thrust upon freshmen at orientation
item.description: 'A young woman bent over while another student pretended to penetrate her from behind,' according to report.

item.title: DEI crackdown, Charlie Kirk murder trial, and more: 5 stories we’ll be watching in 2026
item.description: The higher education landscape in 2026 will include key stories such as the Charlie Kirk murder trial, potential reforms to the left-dominated Truman Scholarship, skepticism towards higher education institutions, and on-going reforms by the Trump administration.

item.title: Harvard whistleblower: White males rejected, institution abandons Western Civ
item.description: 'For now, a better hope lies in building new institutions unencumbered by the corruption and self-hatred that infect the old,' professor wrote.

item.title: DePaul University trains students on how to run pot shops
item.description: DePaul U. trains next generation of pot shops.

item.title: More than half of UC Berkeley disability accommodations are ’emotional’
item.description: At UC Berkeley, over half of registered disabled students have psychological or emotional disabilities. The number of students seeking accommodations has surged, raising concerns about potential system abuse.

item.title: ‘Critical scholars’ fear for ‘gender equity’ after low-ranked man beats #1 woman in tennis
item.description: Nick Kyrgios, ranked 673rd, recently defeated world #1 Aryna Sabalenka in a controversial match. Scholars at Penn State express concern about implications for gender equity, arguing that Kyrgios and Sabalenka's views on male athletic superiority undermine feminist progress. The match has reignited debate on inherent biological differences in sports performance and gender equity.

item.title: After 5 years, teachers falsely accused of Jan. 6 ‘insurrection’ get $120,000 in damages
item.description: Two retired Arkansas teachers, Nancy Best and Cindi Talbot, were awarded $120,000 in damages after being defamed by Sean Allen, who accused them of criminal acts related to the January 6 Capitol riot. A jury ruled Allen's claims crossed into defamation, despite his defense of First Amendment rights. The teachers maintain they did not enter the Capitol.

item.title: Princeton’s ‘champion of anti-racism in classics’ to leave for Arizona State U.
item.description: Dan-el Padilla Peralta, Princeton's notable advocate for anti-racism in classics, is leaving for Arizona State University in August, expressing a desire for public institution teaching. He criticized Princeton’s alignment with community values and emphasized ASU's commitment to inclusion and public service. Padilla aims to expand the study of ancient history at ASU.

item.title: ‘Happiest day of my entire life’: Venezuelan exile who warned U.S. students against socialism celebrates Maduro capture
item.description: 'God is finally giving us the opportunity to witness a measure of earthly justice through President Trump, his cabinet, and the courageous U.S. Armed Forces.'
